en.label: English
en.summary: A Figma interview about using Astra to build a consistent, multi-screen flight-control prototype.

scenes.title: Figma inside and outside the app
scenes.visual: John Milinovich is identified on screen as Senior Director of AI at Figma.

paragraphs.text: This is really sweet. Again, you just think of how much work it did. My goodness, it **built the entire cockpit experience**. I'd love to hear more about what you're working on at Figma. Big part of what we're thinking about is, how do you **make Figma agentic inside and out**? How do you make sure that all of the best models are available to users when they're inside the Figma product? But also that Figma is available no matter where your workflow might start outside of the app as well.

scenes.title: Understanding tasks and accepting direction
scenes.visual: The screen shows written analysis of users, constraints, and journeys for the flight product.

paragraphs.text: What was your first impression on the model? There's **a level of confidence** that I could feel when using it that was a little bit different from anything that I had tried in the past. It felt like it had its own opinion about how it was going to go about doing this in a way that **didn't really require a lot of guidance**. I think in particular, its ability to really give itself time to understand a new task before it actually dives in, something that makes it feel like it leads to far better results down the line. The ability to steer it, to give it direction, even when it was already in the middle of a task was something that felt really special about it.

scenes.title: From a short prompt to a flight-control prototype
scenes.visual: The Figma canvas shows related mobile and flight-preparation screens.

paragraphs.text: I'd love to see some of the things you've done with Astra. Yeah, that'd be awesome. Let's look at it. Imagine you were designing the flight control system for this single person helicopter that was optimized for taking people these short distances. Let's **define some hero flows and some user journeys** that we'd actually build into an app. So kind of what I said is, OK, instead of why don't you actually come up with some concepts for what would make a good prototype and then **actually go and build** this out? You can see, again, it worked for like two hours. Wow. And then built a new prototype for this experience, getting a common brand system in place, using components the right way to actually create consistency, being able to actually do so much work across multiple different screens and actually stringing that together into a journey that would actually show how it experienced this app across multiple surfaces was something that I just haven't really been able to see done before to actually even communicate at this level of fidelity and idea that then started with like a couple hundred tokens.

scenes.title: Design systems and first-principles thinking
scenes.visual: The participants discuss the prototype, component consistency, and planning.

paragraphs.text: I mean, it's pretty incredible because I don't think I've ever seen a model use that many Figma features to like getting everything right from **the design system, the components**, like all of the walkthrough for the experience. It's amazing. In order to do this, well, it would have had to actually **think from like pretty deep principles**, what is required to even set this up right before I actually go and do the design.

scenes.title: Parallel exploration, prototyping, and technical validation
scenes.visual: The guest describes how the model can support the path from ideas to shipping.

paragraphs.text: And what are you personally excited to work on next with Astra? Yeah, I think honestly, continuing to figure out how this is going to **deeply integrate into my own workflow** of and really think about all the ways that this will **impact how we build and ship features at Figma** from that original specification, going from the like messy exploration of ideas to refining something into a clear point of view that we can all line on and actually going through each of those steps of the process to both prototype and communicate ideas visually, but also start to de-risk whatever the most risky parts are from a technical standpoint. Being able to do that all at the same time in parallel is something that there's no doubt is going to massively speed up workflows and just ultimately let us ship a lot more product a lot faster.
